report.text: The API answers 200 OK and the list is in the response, but the app always says 'No items found'. The app reads data.items. The server sends {"itmes": [...]}.
report.hint: Compare the key the app reads with the key the server sends, letter by letter.
report.explain: The server's key is spelled 'itmes', so data.items is undefined. One swapped pair of letters.

report.text: We glued all our JavaScript files into one bundle. Now the page crashes with 'TypeError: ... is not a function', exactly where one file ends and the next file starts with '('.
report.hint: When two files are joined, how does JavaScript know where the first file's last statement ends?
report.explain: The first file's last line had no semicolon, so JavaScript read the next file's '(' as a call on it.

report.text: A CSV import marks 'Mumbai' as an unknown city on 40 rows but accepts it on the other 900. In the spreadsheet, every one of those cells looks exactly the same.
report.hint: If you can't see the difference, maybe the difference can't be seen.
report.explain: Those 40 cells have a space after 'Mumbai'. The check never strips it, so 'Mumbai ' isn't 'Mumbai'.

report.text: After a small edit, app.js won't load. The browser says 'SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input' and points at the very last line of the file, a line nobody touched.
report.hint: The parser reached the end of the file while still expecting something. What could still be open?
report.explain: Something opened in the edit (a { or a ( ) was never closed, so the parser hit the end of the file still waiting for it.

report.text: Our export fetches customers 50 per page. With 1,000 customers it writes 980 rows, and the missing ones are always the last customer of each page.
report.hint: 1,000 customers is 20 pages. How many go missing per page?
report.explain: Each page is cut one item short (say, slicing to 49 instead of 50), so 20 pages lose 20 customers.

report.text: CI went red on a pull request that only fixed a typo in the README. Someone pressed 'Re-run' without changing anything, and it went green.
report.hint: A README can't break the code. So what was different between the two runs?
report.explain: Nothing changed between the runs, so a test is passing or failing by chance, usually through timing or test order.

report.text: Two branches each passed CI on their own. After merging both, the app runs without a single error, but every order now gets the 10% discount twice.
report.hint: Each branch was right alone. What happened when Git put them together?
report.explain: Both branches added the discount in different places. Git saw no overlapping lines, so the merge 'succeeded', but the code now conflicts with itself.

report.text: Our 'orders today' counter resets to zero at 5:30 every morning instead of at midnight. The shop is in India.
report.hint: When it's 5:30 AM in India, what time is it somewhere that matters to servers?
report.explain: The counter resets at midnight UTC, which is 5:30 AM in India (UTC+5:30).

report.text: Checkout fails for some shoppers. People who are logged in never hit it, and it stops happening as soon as a shopper creates an account.
report.hint: What does the code find when it looks up the account of someone who doesn't have one?
report.explain: Guests have no account, so the customer is null and the code reads a field from nothing.

report.text: Our dashboard tab uses 80 MB when it opens. Left open over the weekend it's at 3 GB, even though nobody touched it. A chart on it refreshes every 10 seconds.
report.hint: Nobody clicked anything, yet something grows every 10 seconds. What does each refresh leave behind?
report.explain: Each refresh keeps old data (or adds a listener) that's never released, so memory only grows.

report.text: A job that 'retries the upload until it succeeds' has been running for 9 hours at full CPU. The server it uploads to was shut down last week.
report.hint: When can 'until it succeeds' end, if success is no longer possible?
report.explain: Its only way out is success, which can't happen now, so the loop never ends. It needs a retry limit.

report.text: Typing 30 'a' characters and then '!' into the username field keeps the server's CPU at 100% for over a minute, and then the name is rejected. Shorter bad names are rejected instantly.
report.hint: It does finish, eventually. What kind of check gets dramatically slower with every extra character?
report.explain: The username pattern backtracks: each extra 'a' roughly doubles the work before it can say no (ReDoS).

report.text: The like counter on a viral post says 9,812, but the likes table has 10,000 rows for that post. On quiet posts the two numbers always match.
report.hint: What happens on a viral post that never happens on a quiet one?
report.explain: Two requests read the count at the same moment, both add 1 and both save, so one like is lost.

report.text: A crash happens every time in the release build. Run the debug build with the exact same input, or step through it in a debugger, and it never happens.
report.hint: What do debug builds and debuggers change, besides letting you look?
report.explain: Looking changes the timing and memory layout, so the bug hides whenever you watch it.

report.text: Two threads in our app: one locks the orders cache and then the customers cache, the other locks customers and then orders. About once a month the app just stops responding: 0% CPU, no errors, nothing in the logs.
report.hint: 0% CPU means nothing is working. What is each thread waiting for?
report.explain: Each thread holds the lock the other one needs next, so both wait for each other forever.

report.text: QA says the PDF export is broken on the test server. On your laptop it works every time, with the same data.
report.hint: It works for exactly one person.
report.explain: Something only your laptop has (a file, a font, a setting) is missing everywhere else.

code.hint: No error is raised, yet one charge never reaches the total. Check every name that gets assigned.
code.explain: `totl` is a typo, so gift wrap creates a new variable and the 30 is never added to `total`.

code.hint: No line has a semicolon, but only one gap matters. Which line starts with something that could continue the line above it?
code.explain: Line 3 starts with `(`, so JavaScript reads lines 2-3 as `user.name(async () => ...)` and calls a string. Line 2 needs a semicolon.

code.hint: Picture each item in the list exactly, including anything you can't see at the end of a name.
code.explain: `split("\n")` keeps whatever follows each name on its line, so 'bob ' with a trailing space never equals 'bob'. Strip each line.

code.hint: Count the ( and ) on every line.
code.explain: Line 4 opens two parentheses and closes only one.

code.hint: Work out what page 1 returns with size=10.
code.explain: Pages start at 1, so page 1 should start at index 0. `page * size` skips the whole first page; it should be `(page - 1) * size`.

lines: return sorted(db.orders, key=lambda o: o.created_at, reverse=True)
code.hint: How far apart in time are a and b created? What if the clock gives them the same value?
code.explain: a and b are created in the same instant, so they often share a timestamp. Then the sort is a tie, and the test passes or fails by luck.

lines: # settings.py, right after merging feature/retries into main
code.hint: Both branches changed the same setting, and the merge kept both. Does Python complain?
code.explain: The merge kept both sides' `retries` line. Python silently keeps the last one, so one branch's change is lost with no error.

lines: # the server's clock is set to India time (UTC+5:30)
code.hint: Which clock does each side of the > use?
code.explain: `datetime.now()` is India time but `expires_at` is UTC, so every token expires 5.5 hours early. Use `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`.

lines: // guests can check out without an account
code.hint: Run line 4 for a guest's order, one piece at a time, left to right.
code.explain: For a guest, `order.customer` is null, so `order.customer.email` throws before the `||` fallback ever runs. Use `order.customer?.email`.

code.hint: The chart only ever shows 100 points. How many does it keep?
code.explain: Every refresh adds to `readings` and nothing is ever removed. The chart draws the last 100, but memory keeps growing.

code.hint: Try nums = [1, 5] and target = 5. Do lo and hi ever meet?
code.explain: When hi = lo + 1, mid equals lo, so `lo = mid` changes nothing and the loop never ends. It must be `lo = mid + 1`.

code.hint: Only one pattern matters for '12a50'. Which part of it was meant to match only a dot?
code.explain: An unescaped `.` matches any character, so '12a50' looks like a price. It should be `\.`.

lines: # two ATMs call withdraw(42, 500) at the same moment.
# balance was 600; now it's 100, and 1,000 was paid out.
code.hint: Walk both calls through side by side. Which decision do they both make from the same old number?
code.explain: Both calls read 600, both pass the check, and both save 100. The check and the update must happen as one step (a lock or an atomic update).

lines: // the config usually arrives within a few ms
// fails for some users in production,
// but never while you step through it in the debugger
code.hint: Is 50 milliseconds always enough for a network request? And what does pausing in a debugger give it?
code.explain: It guesses the config arrives within 50 ms. On a slow network it doesn't, so `config` is still undefined. Pausing in the debugger gives the request time to finish, so the bug vanishes whenever you look. Render inside `.then` instead.

lines: cart.total = sum(i.price for i in cart.items)
code.hint: Follow a single call to add_item. How many times does it try to take the same lock?
code.explain: add_item holds `lock`, then update_total waits for that same lock. A plain Lock can't be taken twice, even by one thread, so it waits for itself forever.

lines: # repo: templates/invoice.html. Works on every laptop, fails on the Linux server.
code.hint: Compare the file name in the code with the one in the repo. Which systems care about the difference?
code.explain: macOS and Windows ignore letter case in file names; Linux doesn't. 'Invoice.html' is found on every laptop, but the server only has 'invoice.html'.
